_comment: The FIRST multi-take episode on this format, and it breaks the rule SKILL.md opens with. Critical knowledge 1 says ONE generation per video, never assembled, and that rule is not wrong: it was paid for by five rejections caused by stitching. It is scoped to a SINGLE-TAKE cut. An episode is a different object and the operator approved it explicitly for this run, so the guards move rather than disappear: every take must be one generation with its manifest on disk, every take must be the same model, and every take's prompt must carry the IDENTICAL location clause. check-cut.py's check C enforces all three and still fails a cut with a missing manifest. See SKILL.md 'Critical knowledge 24'.
title: What's in the can
_output_comment: The output name carries all three seeds ON PURPOSE. build_looks.py's look filenames do not carry a seed, and on 2026-09-30 a seed-4816 build silently overwrote street-ld-clean.mp4, which was seed 4815's shipped deliverable. A name that cannot collide is free.
_grade_comment: Not stored. The episode is graded ONCE on the concatenated cut, and the black lift is solved against that file by fit_grade.py at build time (--black-lift, or --fit to solve it here). A grade constant measured on one take outlives the take it was measured on: that is SKILL.md Critical knowledge 19, and the ambience gap made the identical mistake before it (Critical knowledge 13). Grading each take separately would also be wrong for a different reason - three different curves across three joins is a visible step.
_ambience_comment: Not stored either, for the same reason, and this one has bitten twice (Critical knowledge 13 and 21a): the speech-free window belongs to a FILE. build_episode.py finds it on the finished concatenation with the envelope detector and asserts it is speech-free before cutting a bed or an end-card room tone from it.
